## Overview

Often you need to run **the same analysis for several groups**. You could copy and paste the same code three times, but that is slow and easy to get wrong. In this lab you will:

1.  get the plot and the test working for **one** group,
2.  turn that code into **functions**,
3.  use `nest()` and `map()` to run the functions for **every age group**, and
4.  do the same for a regression model.

Write your answers to the questions in complete sentences **in context** and render to HTML at the end.

| Part | Topic                                  | Time           |
|------|----------------------------------------|----------------|
| 1    | Get oriented (data is cleaned for you) | 8 minutes      |
| 2    | One group, by hand                     | 10 minutes     |
| 3    | Write the functions                    | 15 minutes     |
| 4    | Map over the age groups                | 15 minutes     |
| 5    | A model function, mapped               | 8 minutes      |
| 6    | Reuse your functions on something new  | remaining time |

## The data

`NHANES` is from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, run by the CDC. We use the version in the `NHANES` package: 10,000 participants from the 2009-2010 and 2011-2012 surveys.

| Variable | Meaning |
|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `Gender` | `male` or `female` |
| `Age` | age in years |
| `Race1` | self-reported race/ethnicity (5 groups) |
| `BMI` | body mass index (kg/m\^2) |
| `BPSysAve` | average systolic blood pressure (mmHg) |
| `SleepHrsNight` | self-reported hours of sleep on weekdays |
| `PhysActive` | participates in moderate or vigorous exercise (`Yes`/`No`) |

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(NHANES)
library(infer)
library(broom)
data(NHANES)
```

Useful reminders:

| Idea | Code |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| A function | `my_fun <- function(data, arg = default) { ...; return(result) }` |
| Nest by group | `group_by(g) %>% nest()` gives one row per group with a `data` column |
| Map over a column | `mutate(result = map(data, my_fun))` |
| Map over two columns | `map2(data, g, ~ my_fun(.x, title = .y))` |
| Open up the results | `unnest(result)` |
| `infer` pipeline | `specify()`, `hypothesize()`, `generate()`, `calculate()`, `get_p_value()`, `get_ci()` |

# Part 1: Get oriented (about 8 minutes)

The wrangling is done for you so we can spend our time on functions. Run the chunk below. It keeps one row per person (the `NHANES` package resamples participants, so some people appear more than once and the rows would not be independent), keeps adults, and creates the grouping variable `age_group`.

```{r adults}
adults <- NHANES %>%
  distinct(ID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(Age >= 18) %>%
  select(ID, Gender, Age, Race1, Education, BMI, BPSysAve,
         SleepHrsNight, PhysActive, Diabetes, TotChol) %>%
  mutate(age_group = case_when(Age < 40 ~ "18-39",
                               Age < 60 ~ "40-59",
                               TRUE ~ "60+"))
```

# Part 3: Turn it into functions (about 15 minutes)

You just wrote the same plot and test for one group. We need them for three groups (and maybe more later), so instead of copying and pasting, wrap the code in **functions**. A function takes a data frame in and gives a result back. Remember: the code you wrote above becomes the body, and anything that changes (the data) becomes an argument.
